evan: FYI reproduced a perf regression hitting FlashHybrid->paged kernel when KV is interleaved and stride % 32 != 0. ~10% token/sec drop on our internal llama-7b workload :thinking:

maya: ouch. repro script + input?

evan: simple repro: `./bench_attn --model llama-7b --seq 1536 --batch 1 --kv-layout interleaved --dtype bfloat16`

perf-bot: CI perf check: baseline(merged) 1200 tok/s, current-change 1085 tok/s, regression +12.8%

maya: can you paste a tiny profile (nvprof / nsight summary)? curious where cycles are going

evan: gist log snippet:
```
Sampler: nvprof
kernel: flash_hybrid_paged_qkv
elapsed_ms: 2.6 -> 3.1 (+19%)
warp_stalls_mem: +34%
load_efficiency: 78% -> 52%
```

maya: so mem loads are hurting on odd strides. likely uncoalesced accesses when pack stride crosses 32-byte boundary

priya: two quick hypotheses: (1) kernel selection falls through to paged layout for interleaved kv at these seqs and dtype bfloat16 triggers 32-byte misalignment, (2) batching heuristic suddenly increases seq variance and breaks the prefetched KV alignment

david: agree. we saw similar for int8 packing but with bank conflicts. quick mitigation: pad KV to 32 or force separate layout for the canary. can we A/B route?

evan: I ran a micro-bench toggling layout:
- interleaved (no pad): 1085 tok/s
- interleaved (pad to 32): 1190 tok/s
- separate layout: 1215 tok/s

maya: separate looks best perf-wise but memory cost up ~6%

priya: action items:
1) tweak kernel selector to prefer fused/fused-paged variant for interleaved+bfloat16 when seq%32 != 0 (so we avoid the slow path). diff idea:
```
- if layout == INTERLEAVED and prefer_paged: choose paged_kernel
+ if layout == INTERLEAVED and dtype == BF16 and (seq % 32) != 0: choose fused_kernel
```
2) add padding option in runtime to align KV on allocation boundary (opt-in flag)
3) add a batching heuristic check: if seq variance > 20% and many small tails, force separate layout for those batches

david: I'll prototype the selector rule and a canary rollout (dedicated pool). priya: can you add the padding flag + tests? evan: i'll assemble a small reproducible benchmark and include memory deltas

perf-bot: created perf-ticket #INF-7892 with logs and nvprof output

maya: minor note: try not to default padding globally; put it behind a per-model config. we don't want to enlarge working set for all customers

evan: agreed. plan is canary -> monitor token latency and token throughput + mem usage for 24h

priya: also add a small unit in the kernel selector tests that asserts we pick fused_kernel for the edge case so it doesn't regress silently

david: timeline: prototype by EOD tomorrow, canary rollout Wed, telemetry check Thu

maya: sounds good. thanks team :thumbsup:

evan: posting profiler flamegraphs to the ticket now :eyes:
